questions.q: It's 10 a.m. How do you greet your new neighbour politely?
questions.explain: *Buenos días* is the polite greeting for the morning.

questions.q: *¿Cómo te *___*?* — *Me llamo Ana.*
questions.explain: The *tú* form of *llamarse* is *te llamas*.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence: "I'm a teacher" (a woman speaking).
questions.explain: With *ser* + job Spanish leaves out the article, and the job word agrees with the speaker.

questions.q: How do you say "I'm twenty years old"?
questions.explain: Age is expressed with *tener*: you "have" years.

questions.q: Which question asks where someone is from?
questions.explain: The preposition *de* goes at the front: *¿De dónde eres?*

questions.q: *Mis abuelas son *___*.* (Mexican)
questions.explain: The adjective is feminine plural to match *abuelas*, and nationalities are not capitalised.

questions.q: Which word means "why?" in a question?
questions.explain: *Por qué* (two words, accent) asks why; *porque* means because.

questions.q: You meet your friend's grandmother for the first time. Which form of "you" is the safest choice?
questions.explain: *Usted* shows respect to older people and people you don't know.

questions.q: In Mexico you ask a group of friends: "Do you want to go to the beach?"
questions.explain: Latin America uses *ustedes* for every group, so the verb is *quieren*.

questions.q: What does the verb *tutear* mean?
questions.explain: *Tutear* means switching to the informal *tú*.

questions.q: In Buenos Aires, a friend asks *¿Vos sos de acá?* What does *sos* mean?
questions.explain: *Sos* is the *vos* form of *ser*, equivalent to *eres*.

questions.q: Which job word has the same form for a man and a woman?
questions.explain: Words ending in *-ista* only change the article: *el / la periodista*.

questions.q: The feminine of *el alcalde* (mayor) is:
questions.explain: *Alcalde* has a special feminine form, *alcaldesa*.

questions.q: At a market stall: "How much do the apples cost?"
questions.explain: With a plural subject the verb is *cuestan*, and the question word is *cuánto*.

questions.q: The vendor asks *¿Tiene pan?* What is she asking?
questions.explain: *Tiene* is the formal *you* form of *tener* (to have).

questions.q: Someone asks *¿Cómo estás?* Which answer is correct?
questions.explain: How you feel takes *estar*: *estoy bien*.

questions.q: *Mis clases favoritas *___* Arte y Música.*
questions.explain: The subject *mis clases* is plural, so *ser* takes the form *son*.

questions.q: A girl talking about her notebooks says: "*___* cuadernos son azules."
questions.explain: Possessives agree with the thing owned; *cuadernos* is plural, so *mis*.

questions.q: *Me *___* los videojuegos.*
questions.explain: *Gustar* agrees with what is liked; *los videojuegos* is plural, so *gustan*.

questions.q: Your friend says *No me gusta correr.* You don't like it either. You say:
questions.explain: *Tampoco* agrees with a negative statement.

questions.q: At a restaurant, how do you ask for the bill?
options: *¿Nos trae la factura de la mesa?*
questions.explain: The restaurant bill is *la cuenta*; *la carta* is the menu.

questions.q: *Esta es mi *___*: la hija de mi hermano.*
questions.explain: Your brother's daughter is your *sobrina* (niece).

questions.q: *Mañana *___* treinta años.* (I turn thirty tomorrow.)
questions.explain: "To turn" an age is *cumplir*.

questions.q: In a hotel you want to ask where the lift is. Which question is correct?
questions.explain: Use *estar* for the location of a specific thing.

questions.q: Tell your little brother: "Set the table!"
questions.explain: *Poner* has the short irregular *tú* command *pon*.

questions.q: How do you say "It's very hot"?
questions.explain: Weather uses *hace*, and *calor* is a noun, so it takes *mucho*, not *muy*.

questions.q: At the doctor: "My head hurts."
questions.explain: *Doler* works like *gustar*, and Spanish uses *la*, not *mi*, with body parts.

questions.q: In a clothes shop: "I'll take it" (about a coat, *el abrigo*).
questions.explain: *Abrigo* is masculine, so the pronoun is *lo*, placed before the verb.

questions.q: Which is the correct singular of the food called *tamales*?
questions.explain: The Spanish singular is *tamal*; English "tamale" comes from the plural.

questions.q: A woman meets someone new. What does she say?
questions.explain: *Encantado / encantada* agrees with the speaker, so a woman says *encantada*.
